text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Automated alert: elevated GPU driver reset (Xid) rate detected across cluster-serving pool. Error rate crossing paging threshold (95th p90). Auto-escalation -> incidents channel.

alex: I'm oncall, looking. seeing lots of Xid 79/43 in dmesg on two nodes, plus container OOMs. marking as P1.

jin: which nodes? can you paste node names?

alex: node-gpu-12 and node-gpu-27. quick grep from host:```
$ sudo dmesg | tail -n 50
NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, pid=0, Channel 00000000
NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[   24.123456] Kernel panic - not syncing: GPU OOPS
```

sara: ugh. saw a customer-side influx of failed inferences ~14:02 UTC. CS pinged earlier. @cs-rep can you confirm impacted customers?

cs-rep: AcmeCorp and BetaApps reported intermittent timeouts. CS opened tickets 2345/2346. They're seeing increased latency and some 5xx from our hosted API.

mike: on the runtime side, dropping batch sizes won't help if node is hard-resetting. we should drain and cordon those nodes, move workload to spare capacity.

ops-bot: Runbook step triggered: "gpu-driver-reset - triage". Recommended actions: cordon+drain, apply taint gpu:quarantine=true:NoSchedule, scale up fallback pool.

alex: executing cordon now.```
kubectl cordon node-gpu-12
kubectl drain node-gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
kubectl taint nodes node-gpu-12 gpu=quarantine:NoSchedule
kubectl cordon node-gpu-27 && kubectl drain node-gpu-27 ...
```

jin: starting rolling eviction for pods on those nodes. triggering fallback routing for high-latency customers to smaller models. routing change id: r-2026-03-15-01

sara: can we throttle high-throughput tenants to reduce probability of concurrent long sequences? quick config tweak on ingress to set rate-limit back to 80% for non-enterprise.

alex: temp mitigation in place. moving affected customers to dedicated spare pool. watching.

mike: grabbing dmesg + nvidia-smi logs, posting snippet:```
# nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,ERR
Product Name : NVIDIA A100
FB Memory Usage
  Total                       : 40960 MiB
  Used                        : 38012 MiB\nEcc Errors
  Volatile Single-bit         : 0\n  Volatile Double-bit         : 12  <-- suspicious
NVRM logs: Xid 43, 79 entries every ~30s
```

nidhi: double-bit ECC showing is bad. could indicate hardware flake or firmware/driver regression. do we know driver package version?

alex: driver: 535.86, kernel 6.2.12. these nodes recently had a driver rollback patch applied yesterday (deploy id d-1198).

carla: timeline wise, we rolled the patch 03-14 22:00 UTC to ~10% of fleet. Looks like these nodes were in that cohort.

mike: ok hypothesis: driver update introduced an ECC handling regression causing memory parity escalations, leading to Xid/driver resets and GPU disappearing from host, which then causes container restarts and OOMs.

jin: next steps: isolate affected nodes -> image and repro in lab; if repro, rollback driver to previous known-good (533.x) across the cohort, but only after confirmation. meanwhile keep nodes cordoned and drained.

alex: opening incident doc / handoff to eng-runtime for driver rollback. tagging: @mike @jin.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0315-42. Severity: P1. Owner: alex. Playbook link: https://redwood.example/incs/INC-2026-0315-42

cs-rep: CS: informing AcmeCorp they are on our mitigation path; ETA for full restoration est. 2h until rollback validation.

mike: to driver team: can we get kernel-dmesg + driver-firmware dumps from node-gpu-12/27? ssh into host and capture:/var/log/nvidia/*  and /var/log/kern.log. also please preserve VM/core for forensics.

alex: snapshotting logs now and creating support bundle:```
/opt/infra/tools/collect_gpu_bundle --nodes node-gpu-12,node-gpu-27 --out /tmp/gpu-bundle-1823456789.tar.gz
scp /tmp/gpu-bundle-*.tar.gz buildbox:/s3/incoming/INC-2026-0315-42/
```

nidhi: if rollback is needed, we should coordinate with capacity team to pre-create replacement nodes with old driver so we don't induce more instability. avoid manual driver uninstall on live nodes until replacement is ready.

jin: agree. Requesting 4 spare nodes configured with driver 533.x in us-west-2. ops-bot please provision.

ops-bot: Provision request queued: req-8821. ETA ~18 minutes.

alex: handoff to runtime/driver team for rollback and deeper root cause. I will stay as incident owner and will coordinate CS and oncall. If anything changes, @channel update here.

mike: note for postmortem - capture request distribution, model sequence length patterns, whether batching triggers correlated with resets. Also include timeline of driver rollouts (who/when) and canary sizes.

carla: will prepare deployment audit. cc: security for any customer data handling during bundle collection.

cs-rep: customers notified. BetaApps asked for progress updates every 30m.

alex: handing off now to @mike and @jin for remediation steps. oncall handoff scheduled in 45m. will update incident doc with mitigation timeline and customer notices. :white_check_mark:

mike: taking lead on rollback testing. will report back here with test repro or green rollback path.

jin: I'll own runner/provisioning to bring replacement nodes online and validate under load.

incident-bot: Handoff logged: owner->mike, secondary->jin, oncall->alex. Next update expected within 15 minutes.

carla: adding post-incident action item: implement canary watch for ECC double-bit counts and automated isolation when >0.

alex: thanks team. staying available if escalations come in.

(reacts: :eyes: alex, :thumbsup: mike, :pray: cs-rep)
